== More accurate file transfer results in Kobiton CLI

The `kobiton file push` and `kobiton file pull` commands now report file transfer results more accurately on Android and iOS devices.

- *Failed transfers:* File transfers that fail now return a non-zero exit status instead of reporting success. This includes pushing files to restricted device paths or iOS apps that are not installed, and pulling files that do not exist.
- *iOS file transfers:* The `kobiton file push` command no longer intermittently reports an error when a file is successfully transferred to an iOS device.

== Improved reliability in Appium automation sessions

Updates to Appium automation improve consecutive script execution in mixed sessions and attribute handling on iOS devices.

// Source: KOB-55531 from PR #799
// https://github.com/kobiton/docs/pull/799

=== Run consecutive Appium 2 scripts in mixed sessions

Mixed sessions on Android devices now support consecutive Appium 2 scripts without requiring users to exit and reopen the session.

Previously, devices could remain on the *Lightning Mode is turning off* screen after a script finished, preventing further interaction. Additional scripts and manual interaction are now available after a script ends.

// Source: KOB-55522 from PR #774
// https://github.com/kobiton/docs/pull/774

=== Return null for missing element attributes on iOS

The WebDriver Get Element Attribute command now returns `null` when the requested attribute does not exist in iOS native automation sessions, matching the existing behavior on Android.

Previously, these requests returned an HTTP 500 error, which could take approximately 25 seconds to appear because Appium clients retried the request.

// Source: KOB-54317 from PR #769
// https://github.com/kobiton/docs/pull/769

== Simplified tool calls for the Kobiton MCP server

The `userIntent` parameter is now optional for all Kobiton MCP server tools. AI assistants can call tools without providing a description of the intended action.

When `userIntent` is provided, Kobiton continues to record its value in the audit log.

Tool definitions have also been streamlined to reduce the amount of information AI assistants need to process.

For details, see xref:ai:mcp/ai-plugin-mcp-ref.adoc#_call_purpose_userintent[Call purpose (`userIntent`)].

== Access test reports for completed Turbo Test sessions

Completed Appium Turbo Test sessions now consistently display the *Test Report* section in Session Overview. Session details retrieved through the Kobiton API also include the test report download URL.

Previously, some completed sessions did not display the test report, even though it had been generated.

For details, see xref:automation-testing:turbo-test-execution/run-appium-test.adoc#_download_test_report[Download test report].

== Analytics reports

// Source: KOB-55105 from PR #822
// https://github.com/kobiton/docs/pull/822

=== New Mean Time Between Failure report

The new *Mean Time Between Failure (MTBF)* report measures how long devices remain online and available between offline events, helping organization administrators assess device stability and reliability.

Available under *Reports* in Kobiton Portal, in the *Device* category, the report includes:

- MTBF trends over time, summarized by week for a selected date range.
- Average time between offline events, measured in hours.
- A placeholder value of 1,000 hours for weeks with no offline events. This value is not a measurement.

=== More accurate session data in the usage report

The xref:reporting:usage-report/use-the-report.adoc[usage report] now records session counts, session minutes, and validation counts when a session ends instead of waiting for the next scheduled update.

Validation results that complete after a session ends also update the session's counts in the report.

The report's contents and how users access it remain unchanged.

// Source: KOB-55560 from PR #785
// https://github.com/kobiton/docs/pull/785

== Consistent command counts across the Kobiton API and Session Explorer

For Kobiton CLI sessions, the Kobiton API now returns command counts that match the steps displayed in Session Explorer.

The session commands endpoints return one session creation command and one command for each `kobiton webdriver` call, without including repeated session creation requests.

This change applies to CLI sessions recorded after this release. Previously recorded sessions are unchanged.

// Source: KOB-55514 from PR #790
// https://github.com/kobiton/docs/pull/790

== Improved element inspection for iOS screens with unbounded elements

Kobiton Inspector and Appium page source requests can retrieve element information from iOS screens containing elements with unbounded positions or sizes.

Previously, these screens could display an empty XML hierarchy in Inspector or return a `JSON serialization failed` error for Appium page source requests.

Elements with unbounded positions or sizes are returned with a position of `-1, -1` and a width and height of `0`, consistent with Appium behavior. Other elements are unaffected.

The improvement also applies to Appium find element results.

// Source: KOB-55529 from PR #773
// https://github.com/kobiton/docs/pull/773

== Improved image injection for Android apps

Updates to image injection improve compatibility with Android apps and provide clearer feedback when instrumentation is not supported.

- *R8-optimized apps:* Android apps built with R8 code optimization can be instrumented for camera injection without encountering the `Failed to instrument` error.
- *Camera2 support:* Injected images are now applied to camera frames and captured images in instrumented Android apps that use Camera2.
- *Unsupported apps:* When an app uses method handles, instrumentation stops and displays an error identifying the app's file format. Apps that use method handles cannot be instrumented.

=== Appium AI settings require Private device slots

Appium AI organization settings are now available only to organizations whose subscription includes Private device slots.

* Organizations without Private device slots no longer see the *AI Settings* tab in Kobiton Portal settings. Opening the page by its URL shows *Appium AI is not available* with a link to contact your account manager.
* Requests to read, save, or delete Appium AI settings through the API are refused for those organizations.
* Settings saved earlier are kept and return automatically when the organization adds Private device slots.
* Kobiton Standalone isn't affected.

For details, see xref:automation-testing:appium-ai/configure-appium-ai-org-settings.adoc#no-private-device-slots[Configure Appium AI settings for your organization].

// Source: KOB-55557 from PR #803 (Jira status: Deployed) (session reliability on authentication renewal)
// Source: KOB-55562 from PR #786 (Jira status: Deployed) (executor connection handling)

=== Improved Turbo Test session reliability

Turbo Test sessions now handle temporary authentication failures and executor connection interruptions more reliably.

- *Authentication renewal:* Running sessions continue when a scheduled authentication renewal fails temporarily. Kobiton automatically retries the renewal instead of ending the session.
- *Executor availability:* New sessions are assigned only to online test executors. Executors that stop responding are removed from the available pool within approximately 15 seconds.
- *Executor connection loss:* Sessions that lose their executor connection now fail promptly with the status message `Executor connection lost`, instead of waiting up to 15 minutes to time out.

These changes also address an issue where simultaneous executor disconnections and reconnections could prevent new sessions from starting.

// Source: KOB-55190 from PR #820 (Jira status: Wait For Deployment)
// https://github.com/kobiton/docs/pull/820

=== Retained devices included in the Parallel Sessions report

The *Parallel Sessions* report now includes retained devices when calculating peak parallel sessions, even when those devices have no active sessions.

Devices that are both retained and in an active session are counted only once.

Report data from July 2026 onward reflects the updated calculation.

// https://github.com/kobiton/docs/pull/804

=== Session reliability

- Fixed an issue where one unresponsive session could block other sessions on the same host. Previously, new sessions could not start, automation sessions failed, and active sessions could not end until the host was restarted.
- Appium commands and other requests sent to a session that cannot keep up now fail right away with an HTTP `503` response instead of hanging. Retry the request later.

// Source: KOB-55489 from PR #821 (Jira status: Wait For Deployment)
// https://github.com/kobiton/docs/pull/821

=== Scriptless Automation

Scriptless test runs now end sooner when a device can't start the test, and they report the actual error instead of "Device retry exceeded". Previously, these runs could retry for about an hour and a half before failing with that general message.

* Fixed an issue where a run whose app is not on the target device, with no App Repository version to install, retried repeatedly. The run now ends after the first attempt with an *Init session failed* status and the device's error message.
* Fixed an issue where a test case recorded only on the device home screen launched the home screen. The run now ends after the first attempt.
* Fixed an issue where a test case that included a system screen without an app identifier, such as Camera on iOS, failed to start. The run now continues with the other apps in the test case.
* Runs that keep failing to start now end with the last error the device reported instead of "Device retry exceeded".

// Source: KOB-55544 from PR #793 (Jira status: Wait For Deployment)
// https://github.com/kobiton/docs/pull/793

=== Install `.app` builds on real iOS devices in manual sessions

In manual sessions, the *Install Apps* modal now accepts `.app` builds on real iOS devices and stops installs of iOS builds that can't run on the device in use.

* *Upload File* and *Install From URL* accept a zipped `.app` on real iPhones and iPads. A device build `.app` installs the same way as an `.ipa`.
* Android sessions and iOS builds that match the device work as before.

For details, see xref:manual-testing:install-an-app.adoc#_install_ios_app_builds[Install `.app` builds on iOS].
